text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate (hosted-prod). p95->p99 gap widening. Paging on-call.

jamie_oncall: on it. seeing spike on datadog board. p95 ~ 1.2s (baseline 120ms), p99 ~ 6.5s (baseline 480ms). Streaming stalls reported by customers. Paging infra.

maria_sre: added to thread. any logs showing node-level issues? I'm seeing tail latency floor for streaming chunks correlate with gpu-node-73 in us-west-2.

leo_engineer: confirming. our runtime traces show continuous-batching queues increasing and several stream sessions waiting on KV cache fill. One node's avg token latency spikes right before stalls.

ankit_infra: @jamie_oncall @maria_sre I'm SSHing into gpu-node-73 now. quick check:
```
ssh ops@gpu-node-73
sudo dmesg | tail -n 40
```

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-06-11T14:45:21Z for service=runtime finished (no failures)

maria_sre: dmesg snippet:
```
[ 34567.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4321, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 34567.123460] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00 has a corrected ECC error.
[ 34568.000012] thermal 0000:65:00: critical temperature reached: 95C
```

maria_sre: also saw repeated `GPU HANG` and `GPU has fallen off the bus` entries. those map to model-serving pods on that node.

leo_engineer: nvidia-smi output attached (excerpt):
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Temp  Pwr:Usage/Cap | Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
|   0   95C   250W / 300W   |  32200MiB / 32768MiB |  98%      Default |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       
|   4321     python3                32000MiB  C   
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
``` 

jamie_oncall: thermal throttling + ECC + Xid 79 -> hardware flakiness likely. correlate with p99 spikes. tagging severity=sev2 due to multiple customers seeing streaming stalls.

sarah_prod_support: customer-impact: At least 4 paying customers reported streaming stalls and partial responses in last 20m. No complete 5xx flood, but degraded QoS and increased token completion times. Notifying CSMs.

ankit_infra: immediate mitigation plan:
- cordon + drain gpu-node-73
- migrate pods to other healthy GPU nodes
- if capacity insufficient, scale up backup pool or route to quantized model replicas
- open hardware ticket for node 73

leo_engineer: commands run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-73
kubectl drain gpu-node-73 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-73
```

maria_sre: I see pods rescheduled. added temporary autoscale: `kubectl scale deploy/accelerator-pool --replicas=18` to absorb load.

jamie_oncall: temporarily adjusted routing policy to prefer us-west-1 and dedicated fallback pool. Also enabled model-fallback: serving policy routes new requests to quantized-7b variant for a subset of customers with `prefer_latency=true` tag.

leo_engineer: to handle in-flight streaming stalls we also increased gRPC timeouts to give retries a chance:
```
PATCH /runtime/config
streaming.timeout_ms: 90000 -> 120000
```

sarah_prod_support: notified affected customers with early heads-up. internal blameless note: explain rolling hardware issues and mitigation steps.

ankit_infra: hardware ticket created: HT-2026-347 for gpu-node-73. Placed node in maintenance, power-cycled GPU, performing memory stress tests.

maria_sre: monitoring: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 320ms after drain/scale. p99 still has taily events ~2.1s but trending down. streaming stall reports reduced to 0 in last 4m.

jamie_oncall: good. next steps:
- keep node cordoned until hardware team confirms full validation
- schedule postmortem with timeline + suggested actions (better ECC alerting, earlier thermal thresholds, smarter preemptive draining)
- outreach notes for affected customers drafted by @sarah_prod_support

leo_engineer: adding to incident doc and saving traces: `incidents/1748004321/trace-archive.tar.gz`

deploy-bot: incident channel pinned message updated with runbooks: runbook/thermal-gpu-handling v1.4

maria_sre: handing off to @ankit_infra for hardware remediation. jamie please take follow-up for postmortem and customer comms.

jamie_oncall: taking handoff. logged incident ticket: INC-2026-88, severity=2, start_ts=1748004321, mitigated_ts=1748004720 (partial mitigation), impact=degraded latency & streaming stalls for select hosted customers. Will run postmortem template.

sarah_prod_support: customers notified. will coordinate follow-up comms and crediting if SLA breached.

incident-bot: This channel will auto-close the incident thread after 7 days if no activity.

jamie_oncall: thanks everyone :tada: — leaving notes in postmortem; @ankit_infra please update when hardware team confirms root cause (ECC chip fault vs cooling failure).

ankit_infra: will update. current status: node in maintenance, running memtest86 and thermal bench. initial signs point to failing cooling on GPU fan array leading to thermal throttling and transient ECC corrections.

maria_sre: end of thread summary: p99 latency caused by hardware-level GPU degradation (thermal + ECC) on gpu-node-73 -> caused streaming stalls. mitigated by draining node, scaling other pools, and enabling model fallback. follow-ups: hardware RMA or repair, improve ECC/thermal alerting thresholds, review autoscaling buffer for peak events.
